part.label: Flared Hub With Curved Revolve Profile
part.description: A hub that flares smoothly from a narrow neck to a wider base via a curved (arced) transition in its revolve profile, instead of a sharp step -- the kind of smooth, gradually-increasing-radius transition mechanical designers use to avoid a stress-concentrating sharp corner. With an axle bore through it. Curved revolve profiles need extra care versus curved extruded_profile footprints: because the profile sweeps a full 360 degrees around the Z axis, an arc/Bezier through point chosen too aggressively relative to its neighbors (rather than as the curve's own local midpoint) can produce a valid-looking profile that nonetheless fails at the real kernel's revolve() step (REVOLVE_FAILED) -- confirmed by real-kernel testing while building this example. Prefer a modest through point close to the straight-line path between its neighbors, and real-kernel-verify any revolved_profile that uses curve.

components.description: Flares from radius 5 at the base to radius 10 at the top via an arc through (radius 8, z 5), instead of a sharp step or a straight taper.
